{
 "summary": "Findings: 5 actionable issues (0 P1, 3 P2, 2 P3), plus 1 UNVERIFIED P3. The feature works as requested: the user's channel order is parsed and stored in settings-page.ts:8. delivery.ts:24-32 tries the channels in that order and stops at the first one that sends. oncall-feed.ts:6-9 reports the failed channels. I found no Intent Drift. The project has no tests, and nothing in it calls PreferenceStore.set or AlertPreferences except the new settings-page.ts, so the field rename from channel to channels breaks no caller in this repo.

1. Title: Allowed channels are listed twice
   Severity: P2
   Location: preferences.ts:3 (copy of channels.ts:1)
   Failure: Single Source of Truth. `ALLOWED_CHANNELS = ["email","sms","push"]` repeats `CHANNELS`, which channels.ts:1 already exports as the canonical list behind the `Channel` type. If someone adds a channel (say "slack") to CHANNELS, the `Channel` type and `addressFor` pick it up. The settings parser keeps rejecting it as `Unknown alert channel "slack"`, and the compiler gives no warning because a shorter `readonly Channel[]` still type-checks.
   Fix: Delete ALLOWED_CHANNELS and import CHANNELS. Use `CHANNELS.find((c) => c === name)` at preferences.ts:20, or a type guard `(CHANNELS as readonly string[]).includes(name)`.

2. Title: Strategy interface, class and factory with only one implementation
   Severity: P2
   Location: delivery.ts:14-16 (DeliveryStrategy), delivery.ts:19 (FallbackDeliveryStrategy), delivery.ts:36-38 (createDeliveryStrategy), alerts.ts:12, alerts.ts:18
   Failure: Premature Abstraction / Speculative Code / Indirection Tax. There is one strategy and no way to pick another. `createDeliveryStrategy` is a factory that only returns `new FallbackDeliveryStrategy(sender)`. The AlertDispatcher constructor calls it directly, so the interface cannot even be injected or swapped in a test. That is three layers (interface, class, factory) plus a new private field around one 10-line loop. A reader has to follow dispatch -> factory -> class to find the behavior.
   Fix: Replace delivery.ts:14-38 with one exported function `deliverInOrder(sender, contact, channels, text): Promise<DeliveryResult>`, or put the loop directly in `AlertDispatcher.dispatch`. Keep `private readonly sender: Sender` in the constructor. Keep DeliveryResult and DeliveryAttempt.

3. Title: No tests for the new behavior
   Severity: P2
   Location: delivery.ts:22-33, preferences.ts:15-26, oncall-feed.ts:4-10
   Failure: The project has no test files. Nothing checks the core contract, so a regression would go unnoticed:
   - delivery stops at the first channel that succeeds and keeps the user's order;
   - every channel that failed before it is recorded in order;
   - when every channel fails, deliveredBy is undefined;
   - parseChannelOrder rejects empty input, unknown names and duplicates, and accepts mixed case and spaces;
   - the feed text for the three outcomes.
   Fix: Add one test file for delivery that uses a fake Sender failing on chosen channels. Add parse cases for preferences. Add one feed test for each outcome: direct delivery, delivery by fallback, not delivered.

4. Title: "Never empty" is only a comment; the type and the store accept an empty list
   Severity: P3
   Location: preferences.ts:8-9, preferences.ts:37-39, oncall-feed.ts:7
   Failure: The invariant is enforced only in parseChannelOrder, but `channels: readonly Channel[]` and the public `PreferenceStore.set` accept `[]`. With an empty list, delivery.ts:33 returns `{deliveredBy: undefined, failures: []}` without trying anything. The feed then prints "NOT DELIVERED to u; tried " with nothing after "tried". Today the only producer is settings-page.ts:8, which always parses, so this cannot happen under current code. The risk is that the comment carries a promise the types do not keep.
   Fix: Enforce the rule at the type level with `channels: readonly [Channel, ...Channel[]]`, and have parseChannelOrder return that type. Then delete the "Never empty" comment.

5. Title: The feed function sends the alert as well as formatting the line
   Severity: P3
   Location: oncall-feed.ts:4-5
   Failure: Narrow Interfaces. `dispatchForFeed` both triggers delivery (a side effect) and formats feed text. To show a result, a caller has to dispatch through this function, and you cannot format a result you already have without sending again. The doc comment in alerts.ts:21-22 says "on-call page" while the module is the "feed", so the naming drifts between the two.
   Fix: Make it `formatFeedLine(alert: Alert, result: DeliveryResult): string` and let the caller call `dispatcher.dispatch` itself. Use one name ("on-call feed") in the comments.

6. Title: A send that hangs blocks the fallback (UNVERIFIED)
   Severity: P3
   Location: delivery.ts:26
   Failure: The fallback moves on only when `sender.send` rejects. If a send never settles, the later channels are never tried and the alert is never delivered or reported. Whether that happens depends on how real Sender implementations behave. This repo has only the interface at channels.ts:10-12, so I could not confirm it.
   Fix: First confirm whether production senders enforce their own timeout. If they do not, add a per-attempt timeout (for example `AbortSignal.timeout`) and record it as a failure.",

{
 "summary": "Findings: 6 defects (0 P1, 4 P2, 2 P3). The fallback loop itself is correct: a bun probe confirmed channels are tried in the user's order, the loop stops at the first success, and failures are collected. The patch is already applied in the working tree, so line numbers refer to the current files. The repo has no tests, no tsconfig and no callers beyond these six files; I did not run a type check.

**1. Total delivery failure no longer rejects (P2)**
- Location: `alerts.ts:23-26`, `delivery.ts:32`
- Failure: Before the change `dispatch` returned `Promise<void>` and rejected when the send failed. Now it resolves with `{ deliveredBy: undefined, failures }` when every channel fails (probe confirmed). Any caller that awaits `dispatch` for success or failure, as the old contract allowed, now treats an undelivered alert as delivered. Only `dispatchForFeed` inspects the result. No other caller exists in this directory, so the impact on real callers is UNVERIFIED.
- Fix: Make exhaustion an error: throw a `DeliveryFailedError` carrying `failures`, and return `{ deliveredBy: Channel, failures }` only on success. `oncall-feed.ts` catches that error to build the NOT DELIVERED line. This also removes the `Channel | undefined` state.

**2. Single Source of Truth: allowed channel list is duplicated (P2)**
- Location: `preferences.ts:3`
- Failure: `ALLOWED_CHANNELS` restates `CHANNELS` from `channels.ts:1`, which is already the list `Channel` is derived from. A channel added to `CHANNELS` type-checks everywhere, including `addressFor`, but the settings form rejects it as `Unknown alert channel`. The compiler does not catch this, because the copy is typed `readonly Channel[]` and a subset is valid.
- Fix: Delete `ALLOWED_CHANNELS`; import `CHANNELS` and use `CHANNELS.find(...)` at `preferences.ts:20`.

**3. Premature Abstraction: strategy interface and factory with one implementation (P2)**
- Location: `delivery.ts:14-16`, `delivery.ts:19-20`, `delivery.ts:36-38`, `alerts.ts:12-19`
- Failure: `DeliveryStrategy` has one implementation. `createDeliveryStrategy` only calls `new` (Shallow Wrapper). `AlertDispatcher` builds the strategy itself, so nothing can substitute another one. The request asks for one behaviour, ordered fallback. That is three extra names and a forwarding hop from `AlertDispatcher.dispatch` to `strategy.deliver` to `sender.send` with no capability gained.
- Fix: Replace the interface, class and factory with one exported function `deliver(sender, contact, channels, text)` in `delivery.ts`, or inline the loop into `AlertDispatcher.dispatch`. Restore `private readonly sender: Sender` in the constructor.

**4. No tests for any new behaviour (P2)**
- Location: `delivery.ts:22-33`, `preferences.ts:15-26`, `oncall-feed.ts:4-10`
- Failure: The directory contains no test file. Nothing covers fallback order, stop at first success, all channels failing, parser rejections (empty, unknown, duplicate), or the feed line text.
- Fix: Add one test file with a fake `Sender` that fails per channel, covering:
  - first channel succeeds and later channels are not called;
  - first fails and second delivers, with the failure in the feed line;
  - all channels fail;
  - `parseChannelOrder` on `"push, email"`, `""`, `"fax"` and `"sms, sms"`.

**5. Channels with no address are accepted and attempted (P3)**
- Location: `settings-page.ts:7-8`, `delivery.ts:26`
- Failure: `saveAlertSettings` stores any chosen channel without checking that `contact` has an address for it. In the probe, `"SMS, push,,email"` with empty `phone` and `deviceToken` was saved, and `sender.send("sms", "")` and `sender.send("push", "")` were called before email. The user gets no form error for a channel that can never deliver. Each alert pays two doomed attempts, and the feed reports them as channel failures. What a real `Sender` does with an empty address is UNVERIFIED; if it resolves, the alert is recorded as delivered by sms and email is never tried. This is new exposure: the form now invites listing several channels.
- Fix: In `saveAlertSettings`, after parsing, throw when `addressFor(contact, channel) === ""` for any chosen channel, for example `No phone number for alert channel "sms"`.

**6. Feed reporting is fused to dispatch and has two unhandled outputs (P3)**
- Location: `oncall-feed.ts:4-10`, `preferences.ts:8-9`
- Failure, three parts:
  - **Narrow Interfaces:** `dispatchForFeed` both dispatches and formats, and returns a string. Nothing in the change writes to a feed. Any caller that uses `AlertDispatcher.dispatch` directly reports nothing. Whether a feed sink exists outside this directory is UNVERIFIED.
  - **Missing user:** `PreferenceStore.get` throws for a user with no preferences, and that propagates out of `dispatchForFeed` (probe: `Error: No alert preferences for nobody`). The feed gets no line for that alert.
  - **Unenforced invariant:** the comment says `channels` is "Never empty", but only `parseChannelOrder` enforces it. `PreferenceStore.set` is public and accepts `channels: []`; the probe then produced the line `m: NOT DELIVERED to e; tried ` with nothing after "tried".
- Fix: Split out a pure `feedLine(alert, result)` formatter and call it where the feed is written. Type the field as `readonly [Channel, ...Channel[]]` and have `parseChannelOrder` return that, so the comment becomes a compiler check. Decide whether a missing-preferences alert should produce a NOT DELIVERED line; if so, catch it at the same place as finding 1's error.

Choices I made that you can reverse:
- Finding 1 is P2, not P1, because no in-repo caller breaks. Raise it if external callers of `dispatch` exist.
- I did not report raw sender error text reaching the feed (probe: `email (down a@b.c)`), since whether sender errors carry addresses is unknown.
- I did not report the missing per-send timeout; a hanging `send` would block fallback, but the `Sender` contract does not say whether it can hang.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings:

1. Title: A single store only updates the last client. Severity: P1. Location: session-store.ts:21-23. Failure: Single Source of Truth. Constructing two clients with one store overwrites the first attachment. Later sign-in, refresh, or sign-out updates only the second client, so the first sends no token or continues sending stale credentials after sign-out. Separate client-local refresh promises also allow simultaneous exchanges of the same refresh token. Fix: Read the current token from the store when sending, and coordinate refresh at the shared session owner.

2. Title: Old requests can run under a replacement user's credentials. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:32-36. Failure: A request paused in refresh or awaiting a 401 resumes after a sign-out and new sign-in, and send() reads the new session's token. The old user's request can therefore execute as the new user, including its original resource path. Fix: Bind each request to its originating session identity and abort rather than send or retry if that identity changes.

3. Title: A replacement session joins the old session's refresh. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:46-50. Failure: The refresh promise is not scoped to a session. When a new user signs in while the previous user's refresh is pending, an expiring request for the new user awaits the old refresh; if it fails, the new request fails without ever refreshing its own token. A local transport probe reproduced this with only the old refresh token sent. Fix: Associate in-flight refreshes with the session they refresh and ensure the replacement session can refresh independently.

4. Title: Delayed 401 responses start redundant refreshes. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:34-35. Failure: Two requests can send the same token, but if the first 401 finishes its refresh before the second 401 arrives, the second starts another exchange even though the token was already replaced. A local probe produced two POSTs for this sequence. This violates the shared-refresh requirement and can rotate or invalidate tokens unnecessarily. Fix: Remember the token or session used by each GET and retry with the already-refreshed token when it has changed, refreshing only if it is still current.

5. Title: All refresh 400 and 401 responses sign the user out. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:62-65. Failure: The code calls every 400 or 401 invalid_grant without inspecting the response body. A response containing error=invalid_request clears an otherwise current session, as a local transport probe demonstrated. The transport contract allows such a response, and no inspected endpoint contract establishes that every 400 or 401 means revocation. Fix: Clear the session only for a confirmed permanent refresh-token rejection; preserve it for other errors.

6. Title: Expiry fallback is unreachable. Severity: P3. Location: api-client.ts:65-68. Failure: Dead Code Is Debt. parseTokenPair rejects nonpositive and nonfinite expires_in before the conditional executes, so the default never applies. Fix: Remove the fallback, or change the parser's documented contract if a default is actually required.

7. Title: Refresh behavior has no regression tests. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:31-36. Failure: The supplied project and patch contain no tests for proactive refresh, retry limits, concurrent refreshes, or session replacement. The races above can recur without detection. Fix: Add behavioral tests using controlled transport responses, including delayed 401 and session replacement cases.",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings:

1. P1 | api-client.ts:32-36 | Requests cross session boundaries. If user A signs out or user B signs in while A's refresh or GET is pending, the continuation sends or retries the request with the current credentials, including B's token. A probe confirmed an A request resumed as B. Bind each request to its initiating session and cancel it when that session changes.

2. P1 | session-store.ts:21-23 | Parallel State: attaching a second client replaces the first subscriber. Later sign-in, sign-out, and refresh operations update only the second client, so the first sends stale credentials, including a signed-out user's token. A probe confirmed the first client sends no token after sign-in. Read tokens from the store instead of mirroring them in each client; share refresh coordination at the session owner as well.

3. P1 | api-client.ts:34-35 | A delayed 401 for an old access token starts another refresh after a concurrent refresh already completed. A probe produced two refresh exchanges for two concurrent requests. With rotating refresh tokens this can invalidate the newly installed session or cause unnecessary failures. Track the token used by each request and retry with the current token if it has already changed; otherwise join the refresh for that session.

4. P1 | api-client.ts:64 | Every 400 or 401 response signs the user out, although the response body may describe a different failure than invalid_grant. A probe using a 400 invalid_request cleared the session. Check the OAuth error body for the actual terminal credential error before signing out.

5. P3 | api-client.ts:68 | Dead Code Is Debt: parseTokenPair rejects nonpositive expiresIn before this expression, so the one-hour fallback can never run. Remove it or change the parser contract if a default is intended.",

{
 "summary": "Findings: 7 defects in diff.patch (post-change line numbers). The main problem is structural: the access token is now stored in two places that are kept in sync by hand, and the store and client depend on each other. Other defects: an over-broad sign-out, a duplicate refresh after a stale 401, a dead fallback, missing tests and a stale doc comment.

1. Title: Access token copied into ApiClient and pushed back by the store
   Severity: P2
   Location: api-client.ts:14, api-client.ts:22-27, api-client.ts:41; session-store.ts:1, 17, 21-24, 38, 47, 52
   Failure: This is Single Source of Truth, Manual Sync and Bidirectional Coupling at once. `SessionStore.current.tokens.accessToken` already holds the token, and before this change `send` read it from there. The diff adds a second copy, `ApiClient.accessToken`. The store keeps it updated through `client?.setAccessToken(...)` in signIn, replaceTokens and signOut, and `ApiClient` registers itself with `store.attach(this)` from inside its constructor. So the client calls the store, and the store writes into the client. The store has a single `client` slot, so when a second `ApiClient` is built on the same store, the first client stops receiving updates. It keeps sending the old token after a refresh, sign-in or sign-out, including a signed-out user's token. Every future writer to `current` must also remember to call `setAccessToken`. `setAccessToken` is public, so anything can make the copy disagree with the session.
   Fix: Delete `accessToken`, `setAccessToken`, `attach`, the `client` field, the `ApiClient` import in session-store.ts and every `this.client?.setAccessToken` call. In `send`, read `this.store.get()?.tokens.accessToken` again, as the code did before.

2. Title: Any 400 or 401 from the token endpoint signs the user out
   Severity: P2
   Location: api-client.ts:62-64
   Failure: The comment says only `invalid_grant` (a revoked refresh token) should end the session. The code signs out on any 400 or 401 without looking at the error body. Under the OAuth error format (RFC 6749 §5.2), a 400 can also be `invalid_request`, `unsupported_grant_type` or `invalid_scope`, and a 401 is `invalid_client`, which is a client or server misconfiguration rather than a revoked token. Signing out destroys the session, and this triggers it on evidence that does not show the session is unrecoverable.
   Fix: Sign out only when status is 400 and `body.error === "invalid_grant"`. Let every other failure raise the `ApiError` and keep the session.

3. Title: A 401 that arrives after another caller's refresh starts a second refresh
   Severity: P2
   Location: api-client.ts:33-36 together with 46-51
   Failure: Request A sends with token T1. Meanwhile request B refreshes and installs T2, and `refreshing` is cleared back to undefined in `finally` (line 48). A's 401, which was caused by T1, then reaches line 35. `refresh()` finds no refresh in flight and starts a new token exchange using T2's refresh token. The design says concurrent callers share one refresh, but staggered callers do not: N in-flight requests can trigger up to N refreshes. 2. Title: A late 401 on an already-replaced token triggers a second refresh
Severity: P2
Location: api-client.ts:34-35
Failure: The 401 path refreshes unconditionally; it never checks whether the token the failed request carried is still the current one. Trace: A and B both send with T1; A's 401 arrives, A refreshes to T2 and `refreshing` is cleared (line 48); B's 401 for T1 arrives afterwards, `refreshing` is undefined, so B starts a second exchange and rotates T2 away although T2 was never rejected. Fix: Capture the session (or token) used for the first send; on 401 call `refresh()` only if `this.store.get()` is still that session, otherwise go straight to the retry.

Severity: P3
Location: api-client.ts:46-51 (with 54, 64-66)
Failure: `refreshing` is keyed to the client, not the session. If session A's refresh is in flight and the user signs in as B, a B request that reaches `refresh()` (401 or expiring) receives A's promise. On success A's tokens are dropped (session-store.ts:45) and B retries with its unchanged token; on failure B's `get` rejects with `ApiError("/oauth/token", ...)` although B's session and refresh token are fine.

Severity: P3
Location: api-client.ts:5, 66-69

{
 "summary": "Findings:

1. Title: Single Source of Truth: only the last client receives token updates. Severity: P1. Location: session-store.ts:21-23, api-client.ts:41. Failure: attach replaces the sole client reference, while every client caches its own access token. If two clients share a store, sign-in, refresh, and sign-out update only the last one. Earlier clients send no token, stale credentials, or credentials after sign-out. A Bun probe confirmed that the first client sends no authorization header after the second attaches and the store signs in. Fix: remove the token cache and read the current token from the store when sending requests.

2. Title: A request can retry under a different user. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:33-36. Failure: a request sent for session A can receive a delayed 401 after sign-out and sign-in as B. The code checks only that some session exists, refreshes B, and retries A's path with B's credentials. This can expose B's data to A's original caller and changes the request's identity. Fix: associate the request with its originating session and do not refresh or retry it after that session changes.

3. Title: A new session joins the previous session's refresh. Severity: P1. Location: api-client.ts:46-50, session-store.ts:44-47. Failure: while session A's refresh is pending, signing in as B and issuing an expiring-token request causes B to await A's promise. A's result is discarded because the session changed, but B's request then proceeds without refreshing B's expiring token. An A refresh failure also fails B's request. Fix: associate each refresh promise with its originating session and refresh the current session independently after a session change.

4. Title: Delayed 401 responses cause redundant refreshes. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:33-35. Failure: concurrent requests using the same old token can receive 401 responses at different times. If the first refresh completes before the second 401 arrives, the second request refreshes again rather than retrying with the already refreshed token. A Bun probe produced two POSTs for this sequence. This wastes refreshes and can trigger refresh-token rotation or rate limits. Fix: compare the credential used for the failed request with the current credential and retry with the current credential when another caller already refreshed it.

5. Title: Every token endpoint 400 or 401 signs the user out. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:62-65. Failure: the branch claims to handle invalid_grant but never examines the response body. A 400 for another request error or a 401 for client authentication therefore destroys the current session even though neither establishes refresh-token revocation. Fix: sign out only for the endpoint's confirmed invalid-grant response; propagate other errors without clearing the session.

6. Title: Refresh behavior has no regression tests. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:31-36, api-client.ts:46-50. Failure: the supplied project and patch contain no tests for proactive refresh, 401 retry, or sharing an in-flight refresh. These are the requested behaviors and can regress independently. Fix: add behavioral tests covering each contract, including overlapping refresh callers and delayed 401s.

7. Title: Dead Code Is Debt: the fallback lifetime is unreachable. Severity: P3. Location: api-client.ts:68. Failure: parseTokenPair rejects every non-positive expires_in before this expression runs, so the fallback can never be selected. The branch obscures the actual rejection contract. Fix: pass pair directly to replaceTokens and remove the unused default.",

If sign-out or another user's sign-in occurs while a proactive refresh or initial GET is in flight, the continuation sends or retries the original request using the current session, potentially issuing the first user's request under the second user's credentials.  "summary": "Findings: 5 defects in the change (0 P1, 3 P2, 2 P3). All parser claims below were probed under bun 1.4.4 and node 26.13; nothing was edited.

**1. timeZone validation accepts names that are not IANA names**
- Severity: P2
- Location: settings-file.ts:22-23, settings-file.ts:33-40
- Failure: `isTimeZone` asks `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which accepts more than the "IANA name" that the error message and settings.ts:6 promise.
  - `"+01:00"` (a raw offset), `"utc"`, `"europe/lisbon"` and `"EST"` are all accepted and stored verbatim on both runtimes.
  - `"PST"` is accepted on node 26.13 and rejected on bun 1.4.4, so the same file is valid or invalid depending on the runtime.
  - A fixed offset or `EST` silently loses DST, which is the "typo silently does the wrong thing" case the doc comment at settings-file.ts:3-6 says cannot happen.
  - The stored value is uncanonical, so any later comparison or display of `settings.timeZone` sees `utc` rather than `UTC`.
- Fix: validate against the canonical list and store the canonical spelling: `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")` plus `"UTC"`, matched case-insensitively or exactly (author's choice). At minimum store `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en", { timeZone: value }).resolvedOptions().timeZone` and reject offset strings. UNVERIFIED: I did not check that `supportedValuesOf` and `resolvedOptions` behave as needed on both runtimes.

**2. A file saved with a UTF-8 BOM is rejected with an opaque error**
- Severity: P2
- Location: main.ts:18 (read), settings-file.ts:11
- Failure: this is a hand-edited file, and Windows editors such as Notepad and PowerShell `Out-File` write a BOM. `readFileSync(path, "utf8")` keeps it and `JSON.parse` throws `Unrecognized token ''`. The message shows an invisible character, so the user cannot act on it.
- Fix: strip a leading `﻿` before `JSON.parse` in `parseSettingsFile`.

**3. No tests for the new parser**
- Severity: P2
- Location: settings-file.ts:7 (the project has no test file at all)
- Failure: `parseSettingsFile` is a pure function with a stated contract (absent file gives defaults, omitted field keeps its default, unknown key and bad value are errors naming file and key) and nothing asserts any of it.
- Fix: add one `settings-file.test.ts` covering: undefined text, partial object, unknown key, bad `weekStartsOn`, bad `timeZone`, invalid JSON, non-object JSON.

**4. Config directory is hardcoded to `~/.config`**
- Severity: P3
- Location: main.ts:7
- Failure: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is ignored. With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/dcprobe/xdg` set, the file was still read from `$HOME/.config/deskcal`. A user who relocated their config directory gets defaults with no diagnostic. On Windows the path becomes `%USERPROFILE%\.config`, not `%APPDATA%`. Whether "their config directory" means the XDG or platform one is the caller's reading of intent; I am flagging the discrepancy, not ruling on it.
- Fix: `join(process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME || join(homedir(), ".config"), "deskcal", "settings.json")`, and add `APPDATA` only if Windows is a supported target.

**5. An empty or whitespace-only file is an error, not "all defaults"**
- Severity: P3
- Location: settings-file.ts:8-14

This is a judgment call: strict JSON is defensible, but the message does not say the file is empty.

   Severity: P2
   Location: api-client.ts:14, 22, 25-27, 41; session-store.ts:1, 17, 21-24, 38, 47, 52
   Failure: Single Source of Truth / Parallel State / Bidirectional Coupling. The token already lives in `SessionStore.current.tokens.accessToken`. The diff copies it into `ApiClient.accessToken`, and the store pushes updates through `attach`/`setAccessToken`. That makes the store depend on ApiClient, which contradicts its own doc "everything else reads it" (session-store.ts:14). The store can hold only one `client`, so a second `new ApiClient(..., store, ...)` silently disconnects the first. Probe: after c2 was built and refreshed, c1 still sent `Bearer a0`. It got a 401, triggered a pointless refresh (posts went 2 to 3, rotating tokens again), retried with the stale token and threw `/x failed with status 401`. The old code read the store on every send and had no such problem.
   Fix: In `send`, read `this.store.get()?.tokens.accessToken` as the pre-change code did. Delete `ApiClient.accessToken`, `setAccessToken`, `store.attach(this)`, `SessionStore.client`, `attach`, every `this.client?.setAccessToken(...)` call, and the `ApiClient` import in session-store.ts.

2. Title: A 401 that arrives after another caller's refresh starts a second refresh
   Severity: P2
   Location: api-client.ts:33-35, 46-51
   Failure: The request says concurrent callers share one refresh request. Sharing only happens while `refreshing` is still in flight. If request A goes out with the old token and its 401 arrives after request B's refresh has finished, A calls `refresh()` again and spends the new refresh token for nothing. Probe: two concurrent GETs both rejected for token a0 produced `posts after 2 concurrent 401s: 2`. With rotating or single-use refresh tokens this wastes a request and can race other sessions.
   Fix: Remember which session or token `send` used. On a 401, refresh only if `store.get()` is still that same session (or that token is still current); otherwise retry straight away with the current token.

So `pair.expiresIn > 0` is always true and `DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` is unreachable. It also suggests the server may send an invalid lifetime, which the parser has already ruled out.
   Fix: Delete `DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` and call `this.store.replaceTokens(session, parseTokenPair(this.unwrap("/oauth/token", response)))`.

4. Title: Sign-out is triggered by any 400 or 401 from the token endpoint, not by `invalid_grant`
   Severity: P3
   Location: api-client.ts:62-64
   Failure: The comment says the trigger is `invalid_grant` (refresh token revoked), but the code checks only the status code. Under RFC 6749 section 5.2, a 400 can also mean `invalid_request`, `unsupported_grant_type` or `invalid_scope`, and a 401 means `invalid_client`. None of these say the user's refresh token is dead; they point to a client or config bug, yet the user is signed out. The code and its comment disagree.
   Fix: Parse the error body and sign out only when `error === "invalid_grant"`, or reword the comment to match the status-only rule if that is what is intended.

{
 "summary": "Findings: 8 defects in diff.patch (2 P1, 4 P2, 2 P3). The items marked "probed" were reproduced with a throwaway bun script against the real api-client.ts and session-store.ts using a fake transport; the rest are from reading the code. The project has no test files and I ran no suite.

**1. P1: Parallel State / Bidirectional Coupling: the client's cached access token goes stale when more than one client shares a store (probed)**
- Location: api-client.ts:14, 22, 25-27, 41; session-store.ts:1, 17, 21-24, 38, 47, 52.
- Failure: the access token now lives in both `Session.tokens.accessToken` and `ApiClient.accessToken`, kept in sync by the store pushing into one back-referenced client. `attach` overwrites `this.client`, so the store only updates the last client constructed.
- Probe: with clients A and B on one store, A got a 401 and refreshed successfully, then retried with the old token `a0` and failed with `/me failed with status 401`. After `store.signOut()`, A still sent `Bearer a0`.
- Consequences: the 401 retry is broken for every client but the newest, and a signed-out client keeps sending a credential.
- It also adds an import cycle between session-store.ts and api-client.ts, a public `setAccessToken` mutator, and a `this` escape from the constructor.
- Fix: delete `ApiClient.accessToken`, `setAccessToken`, `SessionStore.client`, `attach` and the three `client?.setAccessToken` calls. Restore `this.store.get()?.tokens.accessToken` in `send` (the pre-diff line). The store then imports nothing from the client.

**2. P1: staggered 401s trigger more than one refresh, so "retried once after a refresh" and "share one refresh" hold only for exactly overlapping callers (probed)**
- Location: api-client.ts:34-35, 46-51.
- Failure: `refreshing` is cleared when the refresh settles. A request sent with the old token whose 401 arrives after that starts a second refresh, even though the token was already replaced.
- Probe: two concurrent gets produced `GET /slow a0, GET /fast a0, POST refresh, GET /fast a1, POST refresh, GET /slow a2`. The second refresh also invalidated `a1`, which had just been issued.
- Consequence: under load, N in-flight requests can produce up to N serial refreshes. If the server rotates refresh tokens with reuse detection, this risks churn or revocation (UNVERIFIED: server behaviour is not known).
- Fix: in `get`, capture the token (or session object) used for the first send. After a 401, call `refresh()` only if `store.get()` still holds that same token; otherwise just resend with the current one.

**3. P2: a failed proactive refresh fails a request whose token is still valid (probed)**
- Location: api-client.ts:32.
- Failure: inside the 30 s margin the token is still usable, but any refresh error (503, network, parse) propagates out of `get`.
- Probe: at 10 s before expiry with the token endpoint returning 503, `get("/me")` threw `/oauth/token failed with status 503` although `/me` would have returned 200.
- Consequence: a token-endpoint outage becomes an outage of every API call for the last 30 s of each token's life. The caller also sees an ApiError whose `path` is `/oauth/token`, not the path it asked for.
- Fix: treat the proactive refresh as best-effort. Swallow non-terminal failures and send anyway; the existing 401 path then handles real expiry. Only the invalid_grant sign-out stays terminal.

**4. P2: any 400 or 401 from the token endpoint signs the user out (probed)**
- Location: api-client.ts:62-64.
- Failure: the comment says `invalid_grant`, but the code never reads the `error` field in the body.
- Probe: a 400 with `{ error: "invalid_request" }` destroyed the session (`signedIn: false`).
- Consequence: `invalid_request`, `invalid_client` (401), `unsupported_grant_type`, or a proxy's 400 all log the user out for a recoverable or deployment-side fault.
- Fix: sign out only when the status is 400 and `body.error === "invalid_grant"`; for anything else, throw without touching the session.

**5. P2: a refresh started for one session is shared with callers of a different session**
- Location: api-client.ts:46-55, with session-store.ts:44-45.
- Failure: `refreshing` is keyed to the client, not the session. If a sign-out and new sign-in land mid-refresh, a `get` for the new session that hits a 401 or `isExpiring` awaits the old session's refresh. `replaceTokens` drops that result by design, so the retry at api-client.ts:36 resends the same rejected token and throws 401 without ever attempting a refresh for the current session.
- Related: when the session is signed out mid-refresh, `get` continues at lines 33 and 36 and issues the request with no Authorization header, instead of failing as signed out.
- Traced from code, not probed.
- Fix: the same captured-session comparison as finding 2. After awaiting `refresh()`, if the current session is not the one refreshed, refresh again for the current one or abort if it is undefined. Alternatively store the session alongside the promise and share only when it matches.

**6. P2: no tests for any of the three stated behaviours**
- Location: the diff adds no test file, and the project has none.
- Failure: proactive refresh, single 401 retry, shared refresh, sign-out on invalid_grant and the dropped-tokens rule in `replaceTokens` are all unprotected. Findings 1 to 4 were each found with a fake `HttpTransport` and an injected clock in a few lines.
- Fix: add an api-client test with a fake transport and clock covering those behaviours, including the two-client and staggered-401 cases.

**7. P3: Dead Code Is Debt / Speculative Code: the `expiresIn` fallback is unreachable**
- Location: api-client.ts:5, 66-69.
- Failure: `parseTokenPair` already throws unless `expires_in` is a finite number greater than 0 (tokens.ts:16-18), and its doc says fields are checked "here and nowhere else". The `pair.expiresIn > 0 ? ... : DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` branch can never take the default.
- Fix: delete the constant and pass `pair` straight to `replaceTokens`.
- Related, UNVERIFIED: OAuth servers may omit `refresh_token` from a refresh response, in which case `parseTokenPair` (tokens.ts:15) throws and every refresh fails. Confirm the server contract; if it can be omitted, carry over `session.tokens.refreshToken`.

**8. P3: ApiError message lost the HTTP method, and the store's doc is now false**
- Location: api-client.ts:9; session-store.ts:14.

The change also points readyToShip (fulfillment.ts:5) at this copy instead of the balance (the old code checked `balanceDueCents(order) === 0`). The shipping gate is the decision that must not be wrong. Probe: I recorded a full payment, then popped it off the live `forCustomer` result. readyToShip returned true while balanceDueCents was 1000, and the account page printed "ord_2  Paid in full  ($10.00 due)". That is one line contradicting itself, because account-page.ts:13 reads the live balance and :15 reads the stale status.

That also removes the `Billable` spread in open() (orders.ts:24-30), which exists only to compute the stored field. Derive the status where it is needed: `STATUS_LABELS[paymentStatusOf(order)]` in account-page.ts:15. In fulfillment.ts:5, use `paymentStatusOf(order) === "paid"`, or keep `balanceDueCents(order) === 0`. `Billable` can stay as the parameter type, or the helpers can take `Order` again.

2. Title: A zero-cent (or negative) payment makes an order show as "Partially paid"
Severity: P2
Location: orders.ts:16 (with orders.ts:38)
Failure: paymentStatusOf decides between unpaid and partially-paid by `payments.length`, not by the amount paid. recordPayment only rejects amounts above the balance (orders.ts:38), so `amountCents: 0` gets through, and so does any negative amount. Probe: after a 0-cent payment on a $10.00 order, the account page shows "ord_1  Partially paid  ($10.00 due)" for an order where nothing was paid. A negative amount also counts as a payment and raises the balance above the order total. Customers see a wrong status.
Fix: Classify by the amount, e.g. `const due = balanceDueCents(order); if (due === 0) return "paid"; return due === orderTotalCents(order) ? "unpaid" : "partially-paid";`. Also reject `amountCents <= 0` in recordPayment next to the overpayment check at orders.ts:38. Today that missing check is the only way to get a non-positive payment.

3. Title: An order with no lines opens as "Paid in full" and is ready to ship
Severity: P3 (UNVERIFIED as a supported input)
Location: orders.ts:15, orders.ts:23
Failure: open() accepts an empty `lines` array, so the total is 0 and the balance is 0, which makes the status "paid". Probe: `open("d", [])` gives readyToShip true and the line "ord_3  Paid in full". The old balance-based gate behaved the same way, so this is not a regression, but the new status labels the case as a customer payment. I found no caller that shows whether empty orders are a supported input.

{
 "summary": "Findings: 1 P2, 3 P3. The retry loop, method gating (GET/PUT retry, POST sends once), the retryable status set and the jitter math are correct. `bun test` passes 11/11.

1. Title: Retry-After shorter than the server asked is not "honoring" it
   Severity: P2
   Location: retrying-transport.ts:78 (`Math.min(this.policy.maxDelayMs, ...)`), contract at retrying-transport.ts:8-9, locked in by retrying-transport.test.ts:69-74
   Failure: Intent Drift. The request says to honor Retry-After. When a server sends a 429 or 503 with `Retry-After: 120`, the code waits only maxDelayMs (10s by default) and retries anyway, about 110s early. A rate-limited service will almost certainly reject that retry, so it uses up an attempt and adds load during the overload the header was meant to relieve. The test at :69-74 asserts the early retry (`[0, 1_000]` for a 120s request), so the suite guarantees the violation.
   Fix: When the requested wait exceeds the budget (maxDelayMs), stop retrying and return the response now instead of sleeping a shortened wait. Change :78 so retryAfterMs reports "too long". In send (:62-63), return the response when that happens. Update the RetryPolicy.maxDelayMs doc at :8-9 and change the test at :69-74 to expect one sleep of 0 and a 429 result with inner.calls === 2.

2. Title: Some malformed Retry-After values cause an immediate retry instead of backoff
   Severity: P3
   Location: retrying-transport.ts:76 (`Date.parse(value)` fallback)
   Failure: The doc at :71-72 says a value that is neither seconds nor a date is ignored and backoff applies. Date.parse in Bun is lenient: a probe showed `Date.parse("1.5")` = 978681600000 and `Date.parse("-1")` = 978336000000 (both dates in 2001), and `"2026-03-01"` also parses. Each of these gives a large negative wait, which Math.max(0, ...) turns into an immediate retry with no jitter. That is the opposite of the documented fallback, and it removes the spread the class doc (:38-40) relies on. The test at :91-96 only covers "soon", which happens to give NaN.
   Fix: Parse only the RFC 9110 date shapes. The smallest fix is to require IMF-fixdate with a regex such as `/^[A-Z][a-z]{2}, \d{2} [A-Z][a-z]{2} \d{4} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} GMT$/` before calling Date.parse, and otherwise return undefined. Extend the existing fallback test with "1.5" or "-1".

3. Title: Retry-After waits have no jitter, so stations told to wait retry at the same moment
   Severity: P3
   Location: retrying-transport.ts:63, :78
   Failure: The class doc (:38-40) says jitter exists so stations that fail together do not retry together. But every station that gets the same Retry-After (or hits the maxDelayMs cap) sleeps the same exact time and retries in lockstep. This is the herd the design says it avoids, and it happens against a server that has already said it is overloaded.
   Fix: Add a small random delay on top of the Retry-After wait, for example `wait + floor(random() * baseDelayMs)`, and update the doc and tests. Once finding 1 is fixed, the cap no longer flattens the waits, so this only spreads out short Retry-After values.

4. Title: No test covers the production wiring in createIngestClient
   Severity: P3
   Location: main.ts:6-8; ingest-client.ts:21-50
   Failure: Every test builds RetryingTransport directly. Nothing checks that IngestClient.putBatch and stationName actually get retries, or that raiseAlert (a POST that creates a new alert each time, ingest-client.ts:41) stays at one send. If someone later wraps a different transport or re-orders the layers, the retry behavior could silently disappear, and no test would fail.
   Fix: Add one test that builds `new IngestClient(new RetryingTransport(scripted(...), POLICY, clock))`. Check that raiseAlert on a network error sends once, and that putBatch recovers from a 503 that is followed by a 204.

Not a defect in this diff, noted for the parent: FetchTransport (transport.ts:26) sets no per-attempt timeout. On a flaky cellular link a stalled connection never rejects, so a retry is never triggered. That gap existed before this change.

Evidence: I read diff.patch, transport.ts, ingest-client.ts, main.ts, retrying-transport.ts and retrying-transport.test.ts. `bun test` passed 11/11. A Bun 1.4.4 probe of Date.parse produced the values quoted in finding 2.",

{
 "summary": "Findings: (read-only review; diff.patch is already applied in src/. Behavioural claims were confirmed by running a throwaway bun probe against importInvoices unless tagged otherwise.)

Intent fidelity: the four stated behaviours (whole-file validation before posting, grouping, skipping posted invoices, per-currency totals) are present and work on the happy path. No Intent Drift found. Defects below.

1. Title: Payable-rule failures are reported against the wrong CSV row
Severity: P2
Location: src/import/group.ts:25-36 (throw at :35); enabling cause src/import/invoice-rows.ts:84-87
Failure: parseWholeNumber accepts `-?\d+`, so quantities of 0 or below pass row parsing and are only rejected by createInvoice after grouping, where the error is attributed to `first.rowNumber`. Observed: a file whose bad quantity is on row 3 (and another on row 4) reports "Row 2: Invoice A: quantity of "bad" must be a whole number of at least 1". Row 2 is valid, so the clerk is sent to the wrong line and cannot act on the message.
Fix: Reject quantity < 1 in parseWholeNumber (`/^\d+$/` plus a >= 1 check) so the offending row's number is reported. The createInvoice catch then only covers invoice-level rules (empty supplier or number), where the first row is the right attribution.

2. Title: invoiceTotalCents now silently drops lines that violate the invariant
Severity: P2
Location: src/totals.ts:6
Failure: Dead Code Is Debt, and a fallback that conceals an invariant violation. createInvoice (src/invoice.ts:11-16) is documented as the only way an invoice enters the system and already guarantees quantity >= 1 and unitCents >= 0, so the `continue` has no reachable producer. It also changes a shared function used outside the import: if a bad line ever did reach it, the total would be understated silently instead of surfacing. No disclosure or evidence for the guard accompanies the change.
Fix: Restore the original one-line reduce; keep only the added totalsByCurrency.

3. Title: Unbounded numeric fields post imprecise amounts to the ledger
Severity: P2
Location: src/import/invoice-rows.ts:84-87 and :92-96
Failure: The comment at :90-91 promises integer arithmetic with no floating-point error, but digit strings of any length go through Number(). Observed: quantity 99999999999999999999 with unit_price 99999999999999999.99 is accepted, posted as quantity 1e20 and unitCents 1e19 (the .99 is lost), and the clerk's report prints "USD 1e+37". createInvoice's Number.isInteger check passes for such values, so nothing stops it. A mistyped or malformed supplier value corrupts the payable instead of rejecting the file.
Fix: After conversion, throw InvoiceImportError unless Number.isSafeInteger holds for quantity and for the computed cents (and ideally for quantity * unitCents).

4. Title: Malformed CSV escapes as a plain Error with no row
Severity: P2
Location: src/import/importer.ts:17 and :24 (source: src/csv.ts:39)
Failure: An unterminated quoted field throws `Error("CSV ends inside a quoted field")`, not InvoiceImportError (observed). The file is still rejected and the ledger is untouched, but a caller that catches InvoiceImportError to show the clerk a rejection message will treat a bad supplier file as an internal failure.
Fix: Catch the parse failure at the import boundary and rethrow it as InvoiceImportError, or widen the documented contract of importInvoices to name both error types.

5. Title: No tests accompany the import
Severity: P2
Location: src/import/ (all five new files); src/totals.ts:13-19
Failure: The change adds parsing, validation, grouping, skip-if-posted and totals with no test, and the project has none. Unprotected behaviours that a credible regression would break: file rejected with the ledger unchanged on a bad row, row number in the error, date or currency conflict within an invoice, an overlapping resend being skipped, per-currency totals not mixing, and price parsing of "12", "12.5", "12.50".
Fix: Add one behavioural test file that drives importInvoices and formatImportReport for those cases.

6. Title: Pipeline is a single-use abstraction over plain function calls
Severity: P3
Location: src/import/pipeline.ts:3-17; only use at src/import/importer.ts:17
Failure: Premature Abstraction. A generic class with one consumer adds a file, a type and a module-level constant to express `groupIntoInvoices(parseInvoiceRows(dataRows(parseCsv(csvText))))`. The compiler already checks adjacent stages in the direct call, so the class adds no capability.
Fix: Delete pipeline.ts and inline the four calls in importInvoices.

7. Title: Invoice identity and the skipped list are each built twice
Severity: P3
Location: src/import/group.ts:10 (duplicates keyOf at src/ledger.ts:22-24); src/import/importer.ts:25-31
Failure: Single Source of Truth. The grouping key repeats the ledger's private key formula, so grouping and the uniqueness check can drift apart. In the importer, alreadyPosted is derived by a second pass with `fresh.includes`, which is quadratic and restates the predicate. The report also carries the identity as a pre-joined "supplier/number" string, which is ambiguous when a supplier id contains "/" (observed output "S/1" would render "S/1/B").
Fix: Export the ledger's key function and reuse it in group.ts. Partition invoices once into fresh and posted. Carry `{ supplierId, number }` in ImportReport and join only in formatImportReport.

8. Title: Repeated rows for one invoice within a file are merged, doubling it
Severity: P3 (UNVERIFIED as a defect: the request does not say whether rows of one invoice must be contiguous)
Location: src/import/group.ts:8-24
Failure: Grouping is file-wide, so a file that contains the same invoice twice (for example two exports concatenated) posts one invoice with every line duplicated. Observed: two identical S1/A rows separated by another invoice produced a 2.00 USD invoice instead of 1.00. The cross-file resend case is protected by the ledger check; the same overlap inside one file is not.
Missing proof: whether suppliers legitimately interleave rows of one invoice. If not, reject a key that reappears after its group ended, citing both row numbers.

9. Title: A resent invoice with different content is skipped without notice
Severity: P3
Location: src/import/importer.ts:25
Failure: The skip decision compares only supplier and number.  "summary": "Findings:

1. Intent Drift: Retry-After is truncated. Severity: P1. Location: retrying-transport.ts:79. Failure: A 503 or 429 with Retry-After: 120 waits only the default 10 seconds and retries 110 seconds before the server permits. A local HTTP probe confirmed a 10,000 ms wait. This contradicts the requested Retry-After behavior and can prolong throttling or an outage. Fix: Do not cap the server-specified minimum; if waiting that long is unacceptable, return the response instead of retrying early.

2. Temporary HTTP 500 failures are not retried. Severity: P1. Location: retrying-transport.ts:32. Failure: The retryable set excludes 500, so a transient internal server failure immediately fails a GET or PUT. A local server returning 500 once and 200 next produced one request and an IngestError. Fix: Include 500 among retryable server errors and cover recovery for both applicable methods.

3. Retry-After bypasses jitter completely. Severity: P2. Location: retrying-transport.ts:62. Failure: Every client receiving the same Retry-After sleeps the same fixed duration, including zero, then retries together. This defeats the requested jittered backoff precisely during common throttling and outage responses. Fix: Apply jittered exponential backoff while treating Retry-After as a minimum delay.

4. Malformed Retry-After values can cause immediate retries. Severity: P2. Location: retrying-transport.ts:77. Failure: Date.parse accepts strings that are not HTTP dates. On Bun, Retry-After: 1.5 parses as a date in 2001, and the transport retries immediately instead of using backoff. This contradicts the documented invalid-header fallback and can amplify a server overload. Fix: Validate HTTP-date syntax before parsing and use jittered backoff for invalid values.

5. The public client wiring has no regression test. Severity: P2. Location: retrying-transport.test.ts:36 and main.ts:7. Failure: All tests instantiate RetryingTransport directly. Removing the wrapper from createIngestClient would leave every new test passing while real clients lose retries. Fix: Add an entrypoint test using a local HTTP server that verifies a transient GET or PUT is retried and a POST is sent once.

Verification: 11 existing retry transport tests passed. Local HTTP and Bun runtime probes confirmed the 500, Retry-After cap, and malformed-date behaviors.",

{
 "summary": "Findings: 5 defects (1 P1, 2 P2, 2 P3). The diff matches the files on disk and the 11 added tests pass, but those tests pin the defective behavior in findings 1 and 2. All probes ran on Bun against the real `RetryingTransport`, `FetchTransport`, and a local `Bun.serve` server.

**1. Retry-After longer than `maxDelayMs` is cut short, so the client retries before the server allows it**
- Severity: P1 (Intent Drift: "honoring Retry-After")
- Location: `retrying-transport.ts:79` (the `Math.min(this.policy.maxDelayMs, ...)`), documented at `:8` and `:39`, used at `:62`. Pinned by `retrying-transport.test.ts:67-72`.
- Failure: with the default policy (`retrying-transport.ts:12`, cap 10 s), a 429 or 503 carrying `Retry-After: 120` is retried after 10 s. Probe: `Retry-After: 120` gave a sleep of 10000 ms. All three remaining attempts land inside the window the server asked the client to stay out of, so every retry is wasted and adds load to a throttling server. Typical Retry-After values (30 to 120 s) exceed the cap, so the header is only honored in the short case.
- Fix: when the requested wait exceeds `maxDelayMs`, do not retry; return the response to the caller. Keep the cap only as the limit on how long the client is willing to wait. Update the doc comments and replace the test at `:67-72` with one that expects a single call and the 429 returned.

**2. Malformed Retry-After values parse as dates in the past and cause an immediate retry**
- Severity: P2
- Location: `retrying-transport.ts:77` (`Date.parse(value)` fallback), clamped to 0 at `:79`.
- Failure: the comment at `:73-74` promises that a value that is neither seconds nor an HTTP date falls back to backoff. Bun's `Date.parse` is lenient, so it does not return NaN for these. Probe results:
  - `"1.5"`, `"-1"`, `"+5"` parse to dates in 2001, giving a wait of 0 ms.
  - `"10, 20"` parses to a 2001 date, giving 0 ms. This is reachable: `FetchTransport` (`transport.ts:31`) joins a repeated header, and a server sending two `Retry-After` headers produced `"retry-after": "1, 2"`.
  - `"2026"` matches the digits branch, so it is fine; `"1e3"` and `"120s"` correctly fall back.
  The retry then fires with no delay and no jitter against an overloaded server.
- Fix: accept only a strict IMF-fixdate (e.g. `/^[A-Za-z]{3}, \d{2} [A-Za-z]{3} \d{4} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} GMT$/`) before calling `Date.parse`; anything else returns `undefined`. Add test cases for `"1.5"` and `"10, 20"`; the existing `"soon"` case at `retrying-transport.test.ts:88-93` does not catch this.

**3. Every thrown error is retried as a network failure, including deterministic request errors**
- Severity: P2
- Location: `retrying-transport.ts:56-59` (bare `catch`).
- Failure: the `Transport` contract (`transport.ts:16-17`) says rejection means network failure, but `FetchTransport.send` (`transport.ts:26-31`) also throws `TypeError` for request-construction errors. Probe: an invalid base URL (`ERR_INVALID_URL`) and an invalid header name were each attempted 3 times with backoff before the same error surfaced. With the default policy a misconfigured `baseUrl` passed to `createIngestClient` (`main.ts:6-7`) costs up to about 1.75 s of pointless sleeps per call.
- Fix: enforce the contract at its source. Have `FetchTransport` construct the `Request` (URL and headers) outside the awaited network call so construction errors are distinguishable, or wrap genuine fetch/body-read failures in a dedicated network error class and have `RetryingTransport` retry only that class.

**4. Retry-After waits have no jitter, and `Retry-After: 0` produces a tight retry loop**
- Severity: P3
- Location: `retrying-transport.ts:62` (`retryAfterMs(response) ?? backoffMs(attempt)`). Pinned by `retrying-transport.test.ts:71` (`[0, 1_000]`).
- Failure: the class doc (`:36-38`) justifies jitter so that stations failing together do not retry together. A shared `Retry-After: N` makes every station retry at the same instant. Probe against a real server returning `Retry-After: 0`: three requests were sent within 3 ms. The exponential backoff is bypassed entirely on that path.
- Fix: treat Retry-After as a floor, not a replacement: wait `retryAfter + backoffMs(attempt)`, or `max(retryAfter, backoffMs(attempt))` plus jitter.

**5. Test coverage gaps**
- Severity: P3
- Location: `retrying-transport.test.ts:46-51` and `:88-93`.
- Failure:
  - "never retries a POST" only covers a 503 response. A POST that throws a network error (the case where a duplicate alert is the real risk, `ingest-client.ts:41-50`) is untested; the current code is correct via `retrying-transport.ts:50`.
  - The Retry-After fallback test uses only `"soon"`, which missed finding 2.
- Fix: add a POST case with a scripted `TypeError` expecting one call and a rejection; add the malformed-value cases from finding 2.

**Judgment call, not counted as a defect:** `RETRYABLE_STATUSES` (`retrying-transport.ts:32`) excludes 500 and 408. "Temporary server errors" reasonably reads as 502/503/504 plus 429, so I left it. Confirm if 500 from the ingest service is expected to be transient.

**Verified sound:**
- POST is sent exactly once on both response and throw (`:50`).
- Backoff doubles and caps (`:67-70`); a wait of 0 is possible by design of full jitter.
- The last response or error is returned unchanged (`:57`, `:61`).
- `FetchTransport` delivers lower-case header names, so the `"retry-after"` lookup works against a real server.
- The request body is a string, so resending is safe.
- The `main.ts` wiring is correct.

**Outside this diff:** `FetchTransport` has no request timeout (`transport.ts:26`), so a stalled cellular connection hangs forever and never reaches the retry path.",

{
 "summary": "Findings: (review of diff.patch, which is already applied to the tree; settings-file.ts on disk is byte-identical to the patch. Parser behavior probed with Bun 1.4.4 on 20 inputs. No P1 found: missing file, omitted fields, unknown keys, wrong values, non-object JSON, and `__proto__` all behave as the doc comment states.)

1. Title: Change ships with no tests
Severity: P2
Location: settings-file.ts:7-30 (parseSettingsFile), main.ts:16-23 (readIfPresent)
Failure: Missing behavioral tests. The project has no test file at all, and the patch adds none, although parseSettingsFile is a pure function with several contract branches: undefined text gives defaults, omitted field keeps its default, unknown key throws naming the file and key, bad weekStartsOn/timeZone throw, non-object JSON throws, invalid JSON throws. A regression in any of these (for example an unknown key being silently ignored, the exact thing the doc comment promises never happens) would go unnoticed.
Fix: Add settings-file.test.ts covering those branches through parseSettingsFile(path, text); no production seam is needed since the function already takes text.

2. Title: Config directory is hard-coded to ~/.config and ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME
Severity: P2 (UNVERIFIED as to intent: the request only says "their config directory"; the project has no existing config-dir convention to compare against)
Location: main.ts:7
Failure: SETTINGS_PATH is join(homedir(), ".config", "deskcal", "settings.json"). A user whose config directory is relocated with XDG_CONFIG_HOME puts settings.json in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deskcal/, readIfPresent gets ENOENT on the hard-coded path, and the program silently runs on defaults. That is the "typo silently does nothing" failure the change sets out to prevent, moved up one level. On Windows the path is also not the platform config directory (%APPDATA%).
Fix: Resolve the base as process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set and non-empty, else join(homedir(), ".config"). If Windows is a supported platform, the caller must decide whether to use %APPDATA% there.

3. Title: A settings file saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark is rejected as invalid JSON
Severity: P3
Location: main.ts:18 (readFileSync(path, "utf8")), settings-file.ts:11
Failure: Boundary validation. Observed: text beginning with U+FEFF throws "/x/settings.json is not valid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token" with an invisible character in the message. The file is documented as hand-edited (settings-file.ts:3), and some editors (Windows Notepad in particular) write a BOM, so the user gets an error they cannot see the cause of in a file that looks correct.
Fix: Strip one leading U+FEFF before JSON.parse, in parseSettingsFile.

4. Title: timeZone error message claims "IANA name" but the validator accepts more, and no value error shows the rejected value
Severity: P3
Location: settings-file.ts:20, 23, 34-39
Failure: isTimeZone delegates to Intl.DateTimeFormat, which in the probed runtime accepts "+01:00" (UTC offset, not an IANA name), "EST", and "europe/lisbon" (case-insensitive, stored uncanonicalised), while rejecting "GMT+1", "UTC+1", "". Downstream formatting works for all accepted values (formatEventTime printed correct times), so this is not a functional break, but the message and the Settings.timeZone doc ("IANA time zone name", settings.ts:6) describe a narrower contract than the code enforces. Separately, the weekStartsOn and timeZone errors omit the offending value, so a user with `"timeZone": "GMT+1"` is told only what is expected, not what was read.
Fix: Include JSON.stringify(value) in both value errors. Either reword the message to "a time zone name this system recognises, such as ..." or leave the acceptance as is and accept the looser contract knowingly; do not add a second validator.

5. Title: Missing-file policy is split across two modules
Severity: P3
Location: settings-file.ts:7-8, main.ts:11, 16-23
Failure: Narrow Interfaces, Deep Modules. parseSettingsFile takes `text: string | undefined` where undefined encodes "file absent", so the parser owns a filesystem outcome it never observes, while main.ts owns the read and the ENOENT mapping, and `path` is threaded into the parser only for error text. A caller has to know the undefined convention to use it. The `{ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS }` copy on line 8 is also behavior-neutral for the only caller, which never mutates the result.
Fix: Either make the parser take `text: string` and have main do `text === undefined ? DEFAULT_SETTINGS : parseSettingsFile(path, text)`, or move readIfPresent into settings-file.ts behind one `loadSettings(path)` so main does no settings I/O. Either leaves one owner for the absent-file rule. Small; acceptable to defer.

Checked and not findings:
- Duplicate JSON keys: last one wins (JSON.parse semantics), validated normally.
- `{"__proto__":1}` throws "unknown setting", no prototype pollution.
- Empty file, comments, trailing commas throw "not valid JSON" naming the file; strict JSON is a defensible reading of "a JSON settings file".
- Non-ENOENT read errors (EACCES, EISDIR) propagate with Node's own message, which includes the path.
- main() is exported but not invoked anywhere in the tree; this predates the patch.

Not verified: type checking. tsc 7.0.2 could not run because @types/node is not installed in this directory (TS2688); the project has no tsconfig or package.json. The code ran correctly under Bun.",
